name: Build-and-Find
alternateName: Build-and-Find: An Effort-Aware Protocol for Evaluating Agent-Managed Codebases
description: Release data of Build-and-Find, a protocol and benchmark for evaluating whether downstream coding agents can recover the intended behavior and design choices of a repository written by another agent, and how much inspection the recovery requires. A builder agent receives a hidden specification and writes a codebase; a finder agent is given only the codebase and a specification-traced multiple-choice question bank. The release contains two Rust build-from-scratch task specifications with their question banks, the 48 generated build artifacts, 1,924 sanitized run records (48 builds, 1,728 artifact-conditioned find runs, 144 question-only and spec-only control find runs, and 4 control build records), canonical CSV and JSON tables with a manifest, derived analysis reports, the v1.1.0 post-review layers (question-only control exclusions, transcript audit, implementation-label corrections, option-free check, builder-written test-suite runs, and per-task R_b), and the post-review implementation-label audit records with the author and model-assisted decisions. Each FileObject contentUrl points to the file in the Hugging Face dataset at revision v1.1.0, and each FileSet is contained in the git repository of the dataset, with includes relative to the dataset root. The dataset root has the layout of the code repository root; this file is stored there as croissant.json and in the code repository as metadata/croissant.json.

citeAs: @inproceedings{buildandfind2026, title = {Build-and-Find: An Effort-Aware Protocol for Evaluating Agent-Managed Codebases}, author = {Jhen-Ke Lin}, booktitle = {Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Evaluations and Datasets Track}, year = {2026}, url = {https://openreview.net/forum?id=y48mj8HiWu}}
rai:dataLimitations: The released task pack contains two Rust build-from-scratch task families and is high-prior: question-only accuracy is 97.2% after the v1.1 control exclusions, so accuracy is a validity gate and calibration signal, not a standalone artifact-quality leaderboard.

Conditional inspection effort is an agent-facing proxy for builder artifact quality only after recovery and stability gates are satisfied. Builder orderings are panel-local and conditional on the implementation labels; the two low-effort leaders swap under the adjudicated labels.
Builder-finder affinity is panel-local and diagnostic; it should not be interpreted as a universal model-family ranking.

The agent CLIs ran with permission prompts disabled and without an OS-level sandbox, in per-run workspaces inside the harness repository. 11 of the 72 question-only control runs read files outside their workspace (3 of them answer-bearing files) and are excluded from the v1.1 question-only control; their records stay in the release (runs_release/reports/eandd_final/control_exclusions/). No primary-panel finder read the specification or the gold-annotated question files; the 62 primary-panel runs whose transcripts reach outside their workspace stay in the main analyses, and excluding them changes accuracy by at most 0.11 pp (runs_release/reports/eandd_final/transcript_audit/).

Implementation labels of the 592 scored compile-pass pairs come from finder-consensus prelabels (589) and manual review (3). Post-submission source checks found 9 label errors, and the source-trace audit flagged 205 pairs; under the adjudicated labels 195 pairs move away from implemented-gold. Unflagged pairs were not re-reviewed. The main analyses use the released labels with the v1.1 empty-artifact correction, and the adjudicated labels enter a sensitivity analysis only.
The question banks were written with LLM assistance and reviewed by the author; the drafting and distractor-selection histories were not retained.

Build validation is a compile probe (cargo build --release); the builder-written test suites (runs_release/reports/runtime_tests/) indicate self-consistency, not specification conformance. Runtime correctness, deployment safety, security, and human maintainability require separate evidence.

Empirical claims are panel-local to the frozen builder and finder systems, CLI adapters, prompts, seeds, and benchmark harness recorded in the release manifests. Seeds reproduce harness-side randomization only; closed models and hosted endpoints change over time, so new runs are not expected to be bit-identical.
Multiple-choice Find questions intentionally preserve ordinary software-engineering priors; question-only, spec-only, and option-free checks quantify but do not remove those priors.
Released task content may enter future model training data. Contamination-resistant follow-up studies should use private task packs with the same schema.
rai:dataBiases: The task pack is Rust-only and emphasizes systems-programming artifacts: an SQL-subset database and an HTTP framework.
Question banks focus on source-traceable implementation intent, protocol choices, and failure modes, which may underrepresent other kinds of software legibility.
The final model panel is limited to the recorded Codex and Claude Code adapters and model families; results should not be generalized to all coding agents without new trials.

Implementation-label prelabels come from the consensus of Codex GPT-5.5-high and Claude Opus 4.7-high finders, which are also panel finders; the source-trace audit and the adjudicated-label sensitivity analysis bound the effect of label errors on reported comparisons.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains no human-subject data, demographic attributes, health data, political or religious beliefs, or other personal or sensitive information.

Run records and tables identify synthetic task ids, model ids, adapter ids, seeds, prompt hashes, environment hashes, provider session ids, timestamps, answers, and benchmark metrics. Local file paths and per-run session logs were removed before release, and the release tree was checked for host paths, personal identifiers, and credential-like strings.
Audit records name the author or model-assisted adjudication as the decision source; they contain no other personal information.
rai:dataUseCases: Recommended use: evaluating generated coding-agent artifacts by artifact-evidenced recovery of specification-traced design intent within a calibrated finder-task panel.

Recommended use: validating finder panels, inspecting analysis scripts, reproducing the canonical tables and derived reports, auditing implementation labels, and comparing new agents against the frozen evidence contract.

Not recommended use: certifying deployment safety, security, runtime correctness beyond the recorded compile probe and builder-written tests, human maintainability, public-task-pack leaderboards, universal single-axis model rankings, or training models on the task pack and then evaluating them on it.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset can improve transparency around coding-agent collaboration by making artifact legibility and inspection effort measurable. Misuse risks include overgeneralizing panel-local benchmark scores, treating compile-probe artifacts as deployment-ready software, optimizing agents narrowly for released public tasks, and running agent CLIs with permission prompts disabled outside an OS-level sandbox. The release mitigates these risks through explicit scope notes, controls, label audits, manifests, versioning, a safety note on sandboxing, and separate code and data licenses.
rai:dataCollection: Task specifications and source-traced question banks were authored for the benchmark. Builder and finder runs were collected between 30 April and 3 May 2026 (UTC) with the Build-and-Find harness from twelve agent configurations: GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4-mini through the Codex CLI, and Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, MiMo-v2.5-pro, and MiMo-v2.5 through the Claude Code CLI, each at high and low reasoning effort. Each builder built each task twice (48 builds). Each finder answered the 15-question bank of each of the 48 artifacts three times (1,728 artifact-conditioned find runs), and three times per task without an artifact (question-only control) and with the specification only (spec-only control), giving 144 control find runs. Option order was shuffled per run with a recorded seed, answers were written to a file in the finder workspace, and usage was recorded as bytes exchanged with the model. Builder and finder workspaces were per-run directories inside the harness repository, and the agent CLIs ran with permission prompts disabled and without an OS-level sandbox. Post-review layers were collected from July to October 2026: a transcript check of the artifact-conditioned and control find runs; an option-free check (GPT-5.5-high and Opus 4.7-high, 24 sessions, 96 free-text answers on eight low-prior questions); one run of each artifact's builder-written test suite (cargo build --release and cargo test); and model-assisted source-trace audits of the implementation labels (rebuttal/conformance_spot_audit/ and rebuttal/full_conformance_audit/).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Append-only local run records were sanitized into runs_release/ by scripts/prepare_release.py: records were pruned to the final panel, the controls, and the build-fidelity diagnostics; local trace paths were removed and artifact paths rewritten to release-relative paths; per-run session logs were not released. Repairable malformed or nested answer files were recovered by recorded rules (malformed_answer_recovery_manifest.json and nested_answer_recovery_manifest.json under runs_release/reports/eandd_final/, with the original records kept). Canonical CSV and JSON tables under runs_release/tables are deterministic projections of the records; MANIFEST.json records row counts, sizes, hashes, schema version, and generation time. The v1.1.0 corrections leave the released records, tables, artifacts, and v1.0 labels unchanged: control exclusions and label corrections are added files that the analysis scripts apply. Release CSVs use LF line endings, and recorded checksums are computed on those bytes.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Gold answers: the question banks and their gold answers were written by the author with LLM assistance and reviewed by the author; every question carries a source trace to a specification intention, which bnf specs validate checks. No crowdsourced annotation or human-subject labeling was used. Implementation labels (runs_release/reports/artifact_conformance_consensus/final/): each artifact-question pair was prelabeled when the stable answers (at least two of three trials) of the Codex GPT-5.5-high and Claude Opus 4.7-high finders agreed, as implemented_gold on the gold answer and implemented_non_gold on another answer (696 pairs); the 24 pairs without such consensus were labeled by manual review. These prelabels are triage labels, not independent conformance annotations. v1.1.0 adds one rule-based correction in label_corrections_v1_1.csv: the 15 pairs of the build without source files become absent_or_ambiguous (rule_empty_artifact). Source-trace audit (rebuttal/full_conformance_audit/): after review, a model-assisted source trace of the 592 scored compile-pass pairs (a primary pass and a cross-check pass; models, prompts, session ids, and result hashes are recorded in the audit tables) flagged 205 pairs. Every flag has a recorded decision: 43 by the author (author_decisions.csv; 41 relabeled, 2 kept) and 162 drafted by model-assisted adjudication (two passes, the second without access to the audit verdicts, with arbitration where they disagreed) and reviewed and approved by the author (model_assisted_decisions.csv; 154 relabeled, 8 kept). The adjudicated labels enter the sensitivity analysis in label_sensitivity_adjudicated/. Option-free check (runs_release/reports/option_free_check/): the author graded all 96 free-text answers against a rubric fixed before the sessions, in two frozen passes (claim correctness, then evidence sufficiency); an LLM labeled the same rows for a consistency check that enters only the agreement counts.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The release is versioned. v1.0.0 is the reviewed release, kept as a tagged commit of the code repository; v1.1.0, the version of this dataset, adds the camera-ready corrections as new files and changed analysis outputs, and CHANGELOG.md lists every change. Corrections to specifications, questions, gold answers, labels, or analysis transforms are released as new versions that keep the prior records. Code is maintained in the GitHub repository and data in the Hugging Face dataset; questions and corrections can be sent through repository issues or to jacob.cs14@nycu.edu.tw.
